title: Endocannabinoids facilitate reward engagement through retrograde gain control.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the author manuscript on PMC (PMC13630341); its data statement points to the Figshare author page of David Marcus. Found two Figshare records through the API (31416314 and 31416503, both CC BY 4.0) and listed every file: 5 GraphPad Prism files (0.3–86 MB) plus MATLAB, Python and QuPath scripts, and no raw or per-frame data. Downloaded and parsed 'Linear Track Behavior and 1P analyses for Nature.pzfx': 59 figure tables. These hold per-mouse summaries (5–13 values per column), cue-aligned time-binned % behaviour traces (up to 14,020 bins × 2 columns), and single-value GLM (generalized linear model) and SVM (support vector machine) accuracy results. Also read the SVM README, which says the PCA (principal component analysis) coordinates were made in MATLAB and loaded from Excel files that are not in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the behaviour classifier (a random forest on SLEAP pose keypoints) was trained on 1.4 million hand-scored frames from 45 videos, and that there were 10–12 mice per imaging cohort. These hand-scored frames, the pose files, the videos, the calcium-imaging traces (one-photon Inscopix) and the fibre-photometry traces (GRAB-eCB2.0 sensor) are described in the paper but are not deposited anywhere I could find.

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare records 31416314 and 31416503 download without login under CC BY 4.0. Checked via the API and by downloading one file.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No item-level label exists in the files. The Prism tables are figure-ready group summaries (per-mouse means, time-binned averages). The per-frame behaviour labels, hand-scored or classified, are not deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs are deposited: no pose keypoints, videos, neuron-by-time calcium traces or photometry traces. Only the analysis code that would read them is there.

a4_units_stated.note: The Prism tables carry readable titles (% time, latency, number of bouts), but these are summaries and not model inputs. Checked in the file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The experimental unit is the mouse: 5–13 values per group in the per-animal tables I parsed. The larger tables (up to 14,020 rows) are time bins of group-averaged traces, not independent labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but there is nothing to model.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Per-mouse counts in the Prism tables (around 12 for the Inscopix cohort) agree with the paper's N=12. Checked in the file.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only behaviour labels in the summaries come from the authors' own random-forest classifier. Any label we could take from them would be another model's output, not hand scoring.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from the deposited data: it holds figure-level summaries over about 12 mice, not frames, neurons or trials.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use mouse body-point tracks and brain-activity recordings to predict, frame by frame, whether a mouse is engaging with a sugar-water reward.
plain_idea.train_on: Per video frame: tracked body-point positions, and optionally calcium-imaging activity of thalamus-to-accumbens neurons. The paper describes 1.4 million hand-scored frames, but none are deposited, so the number of usable examples is 0.
plain_idea.predict: The behaviour label for each frame (engage, disengage, walk, rear, groom), taken from human hand scoring of the videos.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Addiction and reward neuroscience labs would get a reusable behaviour classifier and could test whether neural activity predicts when a mouse engages with a reward. That is moot here because the frame-level data is not public.

ml_idea: Frame-level behaviour classification from SLEAP pose data, or decoding of engagement from calcium imaging in aPVT→NAc (anterior paraventricular thalamus to nucleus accumbens) neurons. Not feasible: only Prism summary files and code are deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no item-level data to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the Figshare files (done): only Prism summaries and scripts, with no pose, video or trace data.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A3, A5 and A8. The Figshare deposit holds only figure-level Prism summaries (about 12 mice per group) and analysis code. The 1.4M hand-scored frames, pose tracks and neural traces described in the paper are not public.
